what_it_does: Interlaced Magnetic Recording (IMR) is a hard-drive technology that squeezes more data onto a disk by letting adjacent recording tracks physically overlap — one track is written on top of another in a layered arrangement. The downside is that updating data on an overlapped track forces the drive to rewrite an entire neighboring track too, which dramatically slows write performance. This paper proposes using data deduplication — a technique that detects when two files contain identical content and stores only one copy — to guide where data gets placed on the disk. Deduplicated data that is shared by many files rarely changes, so it is safe to store it on the harder-to-update overlapped tracks without triggering rewrites. This replaces the common but imprecise hot/cold classification (guessing which data changes frequently) with a more reliable signal from the deduplication system itself.
